/-!
# O-minimal theories with a trans-exponential function

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks:
"Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?"

A totally ordered structure $(M, <, \dots)$ is *o-minimal* if every subset of $M$ definable
with parameters is a finite union of points and open intervals (with endpoints in
$M \cup \{\pm\infty\}$).
A theory is o-minimal if all of its models are o-minimal; the complete theory of an o-minimal
structure is o-minimal (Knight, Pillay, Steinhorn). The question therefore asks for an o-minimal
*structure* in which a trans-exponential function is definable.

"Trans-exponential" only makes sense relative to an exponential function, so, as is standard, we
work with expansions of the real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$. A function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is trans-exponential if it eventually dominates every finite iterate
$\exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ of the exponential function. Wilkie's theorem says that
$(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot, \exp)$ is o-minimal, so the question is whether o-minimality is
compatible with definable functions growing faster than every iterate of $\exp$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: O-minimal theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/o-minimal)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- L. van den Dries, *Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures*, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
- A. J. Wilkie, [*Model completeness results for expansions of the ordered field of real numbers
  by restricted Pfaffian functions and the exponential
  function*](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0894-0347-96-00216-0), J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9 (1996),
  1051--1094.
-/

blocks.docstring:
A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of points and open intervals: there are a
finite set $X_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and finitely many open intervals $I_1, \dots, I_r$ with
endpoints in $\mathbb{R} \cup \{\pm\infty\}$ such that $X = X_0 \cup I_1 \cup \dots \cup I_r$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Set.Finite (frontier X)` (equivalent on ℝ but not literal); `Set.OrdConnected`/`IsOpen`; Mathlib has no 'finite union of intervals' predicate.
justification.name: OMinimal.IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints
justification.why_needed: Expresses the o-minimality condition on subsets of ℝ: X = X₀ ∪ I₁ ∪ … ∪ I_r with X₀ finite and each I_j an open interval with endpoints in ℝ ∪ {±∞} (encoded via `EReal`). Mathlib has no such predicate.

def IsTransExponential (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x
blocks.docstring:
A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates
every finite iterate of the exponential function: for every $n$, $f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all
sufficiently large $x$, where $\exp^{(n)} = \exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ ($n$ times).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Asymptotics.IsLittleO`/`IsBigO` with iterates of `Real.exp`; `Filter.Eventually` used directly is simpler and more literal.
justification.name: OMinimal.IsTransExponential
justification.why_needed: f : ℝ → ℝ eventually dominates every finite iterate of exp: `∀ n, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x`. Not in Mathlib.

/-- A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : L.Structure ℝ)
        (φ : Language.ring.sum Language.order →ᴸ L),
        φ.IsExpansionOn ℝ ∧ IsOMinimal L ∧
          ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
            (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.2 = f p.1} ∧
              IsTransExponential f := by
  sorry

Formally: is there an expansion of the real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$, i.e. a

lemma not_isTransExponential_exp : ¬ IsTransExponential Real.exp := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (h 2).exists
  simp only [Function.iterate_succ, Function.iterate_zero, Function.comp_apply, id] at hx
  have : Real.exp x < Real.exp (Real.exp x) :=
    Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp x])
  exact absurd hx (not_lt.2 this.le)

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question (Prop: ∃ an o-minimal structure/theory in which a trans-exponential function is definable); since 'trans-exponential' only makes sense relative to an exponential, the standard reading is an o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field (ℝ, <, +, ·) defining some f : ℝ → ℝ that eventually dominates every finite iterate exp∘…∘exp (for every n, f(x) > exp^{(n)}(x) for all sufficiently large x); the parenthetical '(rapid growth)' is a gloss, not a separate question, and no candidate answer is asserted by the article so the formalization should be an existential Prop (or answer(sorry) over Prop).
claims.reviewer_why: c05 states the standard reading most literally: ∃ language L, L-structure on ℝ, and φ : ring.sum order →ᴸ L with φ.IsExpansionOn ℝ (a genuine expansion of the standard ordered-ring structure on ℝ, verified via pp.explicit to use the intended scoped instance), o-minimality exactly as in Wikipedia (every univ-parameter-definable subset of ℝ is a finite set ∪ finitely many open intervals with EReal endpoints), a total f : ℝ → ℝ whose graph is definable with parameters, and ∀ n, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, exp^[n] x < f x. answer(sorry) ↔ positive existential, all quantifiers on the RHS; compiles under --wfail with only the sorry warning. Other candidates are also faithful but encode 'expansion' only up to interdefinability (c01/c02/c04/c06), via TermDefinable (c08), require ∅-definability of f (c06), or are stylistically weaker (c03 tactic-built structure, c07 @-explicit instances, `AMS 03`). Edits to c05: copyright year 2026, line-length reflow only.

context:
In mathematical logic, and more specifically in model theory, an infinite structure $(M,<,\dots )$ that is totally ordered by $<$ is called an o-minimal structure if and only if every definable subset $X\subseteq M$ (with parameters taken from $M$) is a finite union of intervals and points.
O-minimality can be regarded as a weak form of quantifier elimination. A structure $M$ is o-minimal if and only if every formula with one free variable and parameters in $M$ is equivalent to a quantifier-free formula involving only the ordering, also with parameters in $M$. This is analogous to the minimal structures, which are exactly the analogous property down to equality.
A theory $T$ is an o-minimal theory if every model of $T$ is o-minimal. It is known that the complete theory $T$ of an o-minimal structure is an o-minimal theory. This result is remarkable because, in contrast, the complete theory of a minimal structure need not be a strongly minimal theory, that is, there may be an elementarily equivalent structure that is not minimal.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field with a definable function eventually dominating every iterate of exp; existential Prop via answer(sorry)) match the standard formulation of this question in the o-minimality literature.

/-!
# O-minimal theories with a trans-exponential function

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks:
"Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?"

with parameters is a finite union of points and open intervals (with endpoints in

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: O-minimal theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/o-minimal)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- L. van den Dries, *Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures*, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
- A. J. Wilkie, [*Model completeness results for expansions of the ordered field of real numbers
  by restricted Pfaffian functions and the exponential

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Filter

universe u v

namespace OMinimal

/-- A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of points and open intervals: there are a
finite set $X_0 \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and finitely many open intervals $I_1, \dots, I_r$ with
endpoints in $\mathbb{R} \cup \{\pm\infty\}$ such that $X = X_0 \cup I_1 \cup \dots \cup I_r$. -/
def IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints (X : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X₀ : Finset ℝ) (I : Finset (EReal × EReal)),
    X = ↑X₀ ∪ ⋃ ab ∈ I, {x : ℝ | ab.1 < x ∧ x < ab.2}

/-- A first-order structure on the real line (in a language `L`) is *o-minimal* if every subset
of $\mathbb{R}$ that is definable with parameters from $\mathbb{R}$ is a finite union of points and
open intervals. -/
def IsOMinimal (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [L.Structure ℝ] : Prop :=
  ∀ X : Set ℝ, (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₁ L X → IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints X

/-- The standard interpretation of the language of ordered rings (the language of rings together
with the relation symbol `≤`) in the ordered field of real numbers. -/
noncomputable scoped instance realOrderedRingStructure :
    (Language.ring.sum Language.order).Structure ℝ :=
  letI := Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ
  letI := orderStructure ℝ
  inferInstance

/-- A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is *trans-exponential* if it eventually dominates
every finite iterate of the exponential function: for every $n$, $f(x) > \exp^{(n)}(x)$ for all
sufficiently large $x$, where $\exp^{(n)} = \exp \circ \dots \circ \exp$ ($n$ times). -/
def IsTransExponential (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, Real.exp^[n] x < f x

/--
Does there exist an o-minimal first order theory with a trans-exponential (rapid growth)
function?

Formally: is there an expansion of the real ordered field $(\mathbb{R}, <, +, \cdot)$, i.e. a
language `L` with an `L`-structure on `ℝ` extending the standard interpretation of the language of
ordered rings, that is o-minimal and in which some trans-exponential function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is definable (with parameters)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem o_minimal :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : L.Structure ℝ)
        (φ : Language.ring.sum Language.order →ᴸ L),
        φ.IsExpansionOn ℝ ∧ IsOMinimal L ∧
          ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
            (Set.univ : Set ℝ).Definable₂ L {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.2 = f p.1} ∧
              IsTransExponential f := by
  sorry

/-- The standard structure on `ℝ` interprets the order symbol as `≤`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma orderedStructure_real : (Language.ring.sum Language.order).OrderedStructure ℝ :=
  ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩

/-- The standard structure on `ℝ` interprets the addition symbol as `+`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma funMap_addFunc_real (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.ring.sum Language.order) (Sum.inl Ring.addFunc) x =
      x 0 + x 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The standard structure on `ℝ` interprets the multiplication symbol as `*`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma funMap_mulFunc_real (x : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
    Structure.funMap (L := Language.ring.sum Language.order) (Sum.inl Ring.mulFunc) x =
      x 0 * x 1 :=
  rfl

lemma isFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints_Ioo (a b : ℝ) :
    IsFiniteUnionOfIntervalsAndPoints (Set.Ioo a b) := by

  refine ⟨∅, {(⊥, ⊤)}, ?_⟩

/-- The exponential function itself is not trans-exponential. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
lemma not_isTransExponential_exp : ¬ IsTransExponential Real.exp := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := (h 2).exists
  simp only [Function.iterate_succ, Function.iterate_zero, Function.comp_apply, id] at hx
  have : Real.exp x < Real.exp (Real.exp x) :=
    Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp x])
  exact absurd hx (not_lt.2 this.le)

end OMinimal

items: 'o-minimal first order theory' is read as 'o-minimal structure' (an expansion of the real ordered field): the complete theory of an o-minimal structure is o-minimal (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), and conversely a model of an o-minimal theory is o-minimal, so for expansions of ℝ the two readings coincide. This is the standard form of the question in the literature (van den Dries–Miller, Miller) and the one fixed by the decomposition notes.

'Trans-exponential' is only meaningful relative to an exponential, so the ambient structure is taken to be an expansion of (ℝ, <, +, ·). 'Expansion' is formalized literally: a language map φ from Mathlib's `Language.ring.sum Language.order` into L with `φ.IsExpansionOn ℝ`, relative to a (scoped) instance interpreting the ordered-ring symbols standardly on ℝ (`Ring.compatibleRingOfRing ℝ` + `orderStructure ℝ`). Reviewers should check they are happy with the ring language including 0, 1, − (all definable from +, · anyway).

O-minimality is defined on ℝ only (`IsOMinimal L`): every subset of ℝ definable with parameters (`Set.univ.Definable₁ L`) is a finite union of points and open intervals, where open intervals have endpoints in `EReal` (so `Ioo`, `Ioi`, `Iio`, `univ` are all covered). This matches Wikipedia's model-theoretic definition; the order on ℝ is the real order via the expansion hypothesis.

Trans-exponential is defined as: for every n, `Real.exp^[n] x < f x` for all sufficiently large x (`∀ᶠ x in atTop`). For definable functions in an o-minimal expansion of ℝ this is equivalent to 'not bounded by any iterate of exp' by Miller's growth dichotomy and eventual comparability, so the choice of strict/eventual form is robust.

The definable function f is total (`ℝ → ℝ`) and its graph is required to be definable with parameters (`Set.univ.Definable₂`). A function definable only on a neighbourhood of +∞ can be extended by 0, so totality loses no generality; definability with parameters is the standard convention in o-minimality.

The existential over languages is universe-polymorphic (`FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}`), following the repository's use of `∃ (V : Type*), …` inside `answer(sorry) ↔ …` statements. Mathematically the answer does not depend on the universe (any structure on ℝ can be replaced by a Type-0 language with the same definable sets).
The parenthetical '(rapid growth)' is treated as a gloss, not a separate condition, as directed by the decomposition table.

reviewer_notes: The Wikipedia list entry is terse; every candidate (and the decomposition note) reads it as the standard open question of van den Dries–Miller: is there an o-minimal expansion of the real ordered field (ℝ,<,+,·) that defines a trans-exponential function (one eventually dominating every finite iterate of exp)? This reading is necessary: without the field structure the question is trivial (e.g. (ℝ,<,h) with h a fast-growing order automorphism is o-minimal), and 'trans-exponential' presupposes exp. 'Theory' vs 'structure': the complete theory of an o-minimal structure is o-minimal (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn), so the structure formulation is equivalent. Definability of exp itself is not required explicitly (c06/c07/c08 add it): by Miller's growth dichotomy any o-minimal expansion of the real field defining a non-polynomially-bounded function defines exp, so it is redundant. 'Trans-exponential' formalized as eventual strict domination of exp^[n] for every n (including n=0, harmless); for definable functions in o-minimal expansions this is equivalent to 'not exponentially bounded'. Finite unions of OrdConnected sets (c03/c06/c07/c08) are equivalent to finite unions of points and open intervals on ℝ, so those are faithful too. The final theorem is universe-polymorphic in the language (Language.{u,v}); all instances are mathematically equivalent since ℝ : Type. No candidate omitted the slot; no omission reasons to weigh. The modified lakefile.toml in the checkout is pre-existing sandbox setup, not from me; I built the final file as a temporary module with `lake --wfail build` (success) and removed it.
